rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He gives a third construal of the pronoun: the implied subject is ‘the matter/story,’ namely that the disbelievers’ eyes are fixed when the promise arrives.
rows.anchor: وقد يكون التقدير في الآية: فإذا القصة شاخصة أبصار الذين كفروا

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī says the disbelievers’ eyes stare without nearly blinking from the day’s terror and severity.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: شخصت أبصار الكفار فلا تكاد تطرف من شدة ذلك اليوم وهوله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains their confession of heedlessness as their worldly blindness to what was required of them.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد في الدنيا كنا في عماية عما يراد منا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their admission that they were wrongdoers means they wronged themselves by denying Muḥammad and taking deities.
rows.anchor: أنفسنا بتكذيب محمد -صلى الله عليه وسلم- واتخاذ الآلهة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās takes the address as directed to the people of Mecca.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد أهل مكة

words: إِن كُنتُمْ فِى رَيْبٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلْبَعْثِ
rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abū Isḥāq says the verse addresses polytheists who denied resurrection and were in doubt about it.
rows.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: قيل للذين جحدوا البعث وهم المشركون إن كنتم في شك من

words: إِن كُنتُمْ فِى رَيْبٍۢ مِّنَ ٱلْبَعْثِ
rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abū Isḥāq says the deniers should reflect on their beginning: divine power does not differ between initiating creation and restoring it.
rows.anchor: أن الله يبعث الموتى فتدبروا أمر خلقكم وابتدائكم فإنكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author lays out the sequence: Adam from soil, then his descendants from a sperm-drop, a clot, and a morsel, thereby showing their creation stages.
rows.anchor: أنهم خلقوا من تراب، وهو خلق آدم

rows.speaker: صاحب النظم
rows.claim: The author of al-Naẓm paraphrases the argument: if you doubt resurrection, God informs you that He created you from dust.
rows.anchor: صاحب النظم: معنى الآية إن كنتم في ريب من البعث فإنا نخبركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here the sperm-drop means the child of Adam, formed from the father’s semen; Arabic calls a small amount of water nuṭfa.
rows.anchor: والذي يخلق منه الولد يسمى نطفة، لأنه ماء يقطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nuṭfa derives from dripping: it can mean a clear remnant of water, a cloud’s dripping, or rain lasting through the night; semen is so named because it drips.
rows.anchor: في الغدير نطفة زرقاء، أي بقية ماء صاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAlaqa is thick, congealed blood before it dries, and a piece of that blood; the cited al-Qaṭāmī line witnesses the word ʿalaq.
rows.anchor: العلق الدم الجامد قبل أن ييبس، والقطعة علقة منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The drop that forms a child thickens into blood; when the clot becomes flesh it is a muḍgha, a piece of flesh, as the human heart is a bodily morsel.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن النطفة المخلوق منها الولد تصير دما غليظا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses muḍgha as flesh.
rows.anchor: فهي مضغة. قال ابن عباس. يريد من

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith cited here says each stage lasts forty days—drop, clot, then morsel—after which an angel is sent to breathe in the spirit.
rows.anchor: وهذا كله في الأطوار أربعة أشهر، وهذا معنى ما روي في الحديث:

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the fetus is formed during the ten days after four months, then receives the spirit; this explains the widow’s four months and ten days of waiting, and movement signals pregnancy.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: [ثم يصور]

rows.speaker: ابن الأعرابي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Aʿrābī says mukhallaqa is a stage whose form has begun to appear, while ghayr mukhallaqa has not yet been shaped.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الأعرابي: {مخلقة} قد بدا خلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author identifies Ibn al-Aʿrābī’s explanation of mukhallaqa as the word’s lexical sense.
rows.anchor: هو معنى المخلقة في اللغة.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid, in Ibn Nujaḥ’s transmission, says the words describe miscarriage: a miscarried fetus is both formed and unformed.
rows.anchor: مجاهد -في رواية ابن نجيح- {مخلقة وغير مخلقة} قال: السقط مخلوق وغير مخلوق

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī details the miscarriage stages: a woman may miscarry a drop, a clot, unformed flesh, partly formed flesh, or a fully formed fetus.
rows.anchor: السدي عن هذا المعنى الذي ذكره مجاهد فقال: هذا في السقط

words: وَنُقِرُّ فِى ٱلْأَرْحَامِ مَا نَشَآءُ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍۢ مُّسَمًّۭى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He supports the miscarriage interpretation by reading ‘We establish in wombs what We will’ as what reaches its full term rather than being miscarried.
rows.anchor: قوله {ونقر في الأرحام ما نشاء}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says mukhallaqa is what lives and ghayr mukhallaqa is miscarriage.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس -في رواية عكرمة-: المخلقة ما

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid, in Khusayf’s transmission, identifies mukhallaqa as the child and ghayr mukhallaqa as miscarriage.
rows.anchor: مجاهد -في رواية خصيف- قال: المخلقة: الولد،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, in ʿAṭāʾ’s transmission, says the formed fetus is one for whom the covenant was taken, whereas the unformed one had no covenant and is not created.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: المخلقة: ما

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Alqama reports from Ibn Masʿūd that an angel asks whether the drop is formed; if not, the womb expels it, but if so, the angel records sex, provision, lifespan, and destiny from the Preserved Book.
rows.anchor: روى علقمة، عن عبد الله بن مسعود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He takes mukhallaqa here as fully created through the breathing of the spirit: a fetus completed alive goes to term, while miscarriage is incomplete in this sense.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا القول معنى (المخلقة): المخلوقة كما ذكره ابن عباس -في رواية عطاء-

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbī glosses the pair as created and uncreated: a full-term child is created, and miscarriage is uncreated; the author says this is most commentators’ view and notes Abū ʿUbayda agrees.
rows.anchor: الكلبي: {مخلقة وغير مخلقة} يقول مخلوق وغير مخلوق

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda understands mukhallaqa and ghayr mukhallaqa as complete and incomplete; Abū Isḥāq and Thaʿlab choose this interpretation, which concerns born children rather than miscarriage.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة في قوله {مخلقة وغير مخلقة}: تامة وغير تامة

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abū Isḥāq says some morsels complete their human organs and faculties, while God does not complete the formation of others.
rows.anchor: أبو إسحاق: وصف أحوال الخلق أن منهم من يتم

rows.speaker: أبو العباس
rows.claim: Abū al-ʿAbbās says people are of two kinds: fully formed or deficient and incomplete.
rows.anchor: الناس خلقوا على ضربين: منهم تام الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the third interpretation, mukhallaqa means complete in bodily form and limbs; the author summarizes three interpretations of mukhallaqa.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا القول معنى المخلقة: التام الخلقة والأعضاء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the purpose is to show people what they should do and leave, and to distinguish the best of them and what worship requires.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس: لنبين لكم ما تأتون وما تذرون

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the stages of human creation demonstrate God’s power to do as He wills and inform people how He first created them.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: أي. ذكرنا أحوال خلق الإنسان

rows.speaker: صاحب النظم
rows.claim: The author of al-Naẓm says the purpose is to make clear that resurrection is true, since the verse was revealed as evidence for resurrection.
rows.anchor: صاحب النظم: لنبين لكم أن البعث حق يدل على هذا

rows.speaker: ابن مسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Muslim takes the purpose as showing how God creates people in the wombs.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن مسلم: لنبين لكم كيف نخلقكم في الأرحام

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: The scholars of meaning say the varied forms of creation point people to God’s power to bring about what He can do.
rows.anchor: أهل المعاني: لندلكم على مقدورنا بتصريف ضروب الخلق

words: وَنُقِرُّ فِى ٱلْأَرْحَامِ مَا نَشَآءُ إِلَىٰٓ أَجَلٍۢ مُّسَمًّۭى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means God keeps in the womb what He wills rather than letting it miscarry until the appointed birth term.
rows.anchor: في الأرحام ما نشاء فلا يكون سقطا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God does not let the fetus leave before its customary term, which He decreed for it in the Preserved Book; pregnancies range from six months to four years.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المعنى: {ونقر في الأرحام ما نشاء} فلا يخرج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The usual reading of ونقرُّ has the verb in the indicative; al-Mufaḍḍal reports ʿĀṣim’s accusative reading ونقرَ.
rows.anchor: والقراءة في "ونقر" بالرفع، وروى المفضل

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abū Isḥāq rejects the accusative: God did not create humanity in order to keep people in wombs, but to guide them toward right guidance and good conduct.
rows.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: ولا يجوز فيه إلا الرفع

rows.speaker: صاحب النظم
rows.claim: The author of al-Naẓm treats ونقر as a new independent statement after the clause ending at لنبين لكم, explaining its indicative mood.
rows.anchor: صاحب النظم: انقطع الخبر عند قوله {لنبين لكم}

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says ṭiflan has plural sense, supported by the plural address; understood distributively, it means each of you is brought out as a child.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: "طفلا" في معنى أطفال

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad parses ṭiflan as a verbal noun functioning circumstantially; others call it specification, which is possible, as in the cited construction.
rows.anchor: وقال المبرد: انتصب "طفلا" على المصدر الذي هو في موضع الحال.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author supports the verbal-noun analysis by noting that the form occurs as a verbal noun like riḍā and ʿadl; the child wording in 24:31 is evidence.
rows.anchor: إلا أنا قدمنا المصدر؛ لأنه قد استعمل مصدرا كالرضا والعدل

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbayda also takes ṭiflan to stand for a plural, a usage he illustrates with a line of poetry.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: طفلا في موضع أطفال

rows.speaker: أبو الهيثم
rows.claim: Abū al-Haytham says a child is called ṭifl from birth until puberty; Arabic uses the same form for singular, dual, and plural feminine or masculine cases, but not ṭiflat.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو الهيثم: الصبي يدعى طفلا حين يسقط من بطن أمه إلى أن يحتلم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author gives the further forms ṭifl, ṭifla, dual ṭiflān/ṭiflatān, and aṭfāl, and says a woman or gazelle ‘has a child’ when she becomes mother to one.
rows.anchor: جارية طفل، وجاريتان طفل، وجوار طفل

rows.speaker: صاحب النظم
rows.claim: The author of al-Naẓm gives two constructions: omit ‘then We make you live’ before reaching maturity, or treat the second ثم as extra, yielding ‘We bring you out children to reach maturity.’
rows.anchor: ذكر صاحب النظم منه وجهين: أحدهما: أن يكون فيه إضمار

rows.speaker: صاحب النظم
rows.claim: His second construction regards ثم as inserted, like a coordinating wāw, so the sense is that people are brought out as children to attain maturity.
rows.anchor: والوجه الآخر: أن تكون "ثم" في قوله {ثم لتبلغوا} مقحمة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the age of full maturity as eighteen years.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد ثماني عشرة سنة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj defines full maturity as completeness, strength, and discernment, placing it between thirty and forty.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: وتأويله الكمال والقوة والتمييز وهو ما بين الثلاثين إلى الأربعين

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains that some people die before reaching full maturity.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد من قبل ذلك. يعني من قبل بلوغ الأشد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ardhal al-ʿumur is the lowest, most decrepit age: senility, when a person becomes confused and loses the ability to reason.
rows.anchor: أي: أخسه وأدونه، وهو الخرف

words: لِكَيْلَا يَعْلَمَ مِنۢ بَعْدِ عِلْمٍۢ شَيْـًۭٔا
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says this is when age changes a person’s mind until he no longer understands anything, and says it occurs only among polytheists.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد يبلغ من السن ما يتغير

words: لِكَيْلَا يَعْلَمَ مِنۢ بَعْدِ عِلْمٍۢ شَيْـًۭٔا
rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima says a Qurʾān reciter will not reach this state, citing the exception in 95:5–6 and interpreting those who believe and act righteously as Qurʾān readers.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة: من قرأ القرآن لم يصر بهذه الحالة، واحتج بقوله: {ثم رددناه أسفل سافلين

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says God demonstrates His power to revive the dead by reviving the earth.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: ثم دلهم على إحيائه

rows.speaker: صاحب النظم
rows.claim: The author of al-Naẓm calls this a separate passage because it shifts from addressing a group to one person, but says it remains linked as evidence for resurrection.
rows.anchor: وقال صاحب النظم: هذا فصل منقطع مما قبله؛ لأن الأول مخاطبة جماعة وهذا مخاطبة واحد

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: Al-Layth defines hāmida as hard, crusted earth without vegetation except broken dry remnants; a hāmid plant is dry.
rows.anchor: قال الليث: أرض جامدة مقشعرة لا نبات فيها إلا يبيس

rows.speaker: شمر
rows.claim: Shammar says hāmid is barren land without life; he also uses the root for settled, layered ash and cloth crumbling from wear.
rows.anchor: وقال شمر: الهامد: الأرض المسنتة

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī says a fire hamadat when it went out completely; the cited al-Aʿshā line uses hamdan of worn-out clothes.
rows.anchor: النار إذا طفئت ألبتة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the earth has settled and lost its moisture.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: هامدة يريد التي قد تلبدت وذهب عنها النذى

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid calls it perished, meaning dry and parched, since the earth’s death is its dryness.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: هالكة. يعني جافة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda describes it as gray and broken, meaning its vegetation is shattered.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: غبراء متهشمة

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abū Isḥāq says the earth is dry and covered with soil.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: يعني جافة ذات تراب

rows.speaker: ابن مسلم
rows.claim: Ibn Muslim describes it as dead and dry, like a fire extinguished and gone.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن مسلم: ميتة يابسة كالنار إذا طفئت فذهبت

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The commentators say the earth moves with vegetation when water falls; it rises and swells as growth appears.
rows.anchor: المعنى على هذا تحركت بالنبات عند وقوع الماء

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: Al-Layth says the expression ‘the earth trembled’ is used when it sprouts.
rows.anchor: وقال الليث: يقال اهتزت الأرض

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad supplies an ellipsis: ‘its vegetation trembled’; this is more apparent because vegetation is said to tremble when it grows tall.
rows.anchor: والاهتزاز في النبات أظهر، ويقال: اهتز النبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rabat means increased and grew, referring either to the earth or its plants; the root also yields rabwa and ribā.
rows.anchor: وقوله {وربت} أي زادت ونمت

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses every pair or kind as beautiful; bahja is beauty and freshness, and bahīj is beautiful to look at and pleasing to the eye.
rows.anchor: ابن عباس: من كل صنف حسن

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad defines bahīj as something bright and beautiful, connecting it with ‘gardens of beauty’ in 27:60.
rows.anchor: قال المبرد: هو الشيء المشرق الجميل

rows.speaker: أبو زيد
rows.claim: Abū Zayd analyzes bahīj as an adjective from bahija, meaning beautiful, and notes the related forms bahāja and bahja.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا هو فعيل من بهج

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: Al-Layth cites tabāhaja al-rawḍ when a meadow fills with blossoms, with a poetic line describing its blossoms as resplendent.
rows.anchor: ويقال: تباهج الروض إذا كثر نواره

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: Most grammarians, including al-Akhfash and Ibn Muslim, parse bahīj here as an active-participle form.
rows.anchor: النحو على أن بهيج هاهنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who associate partners with God are the Arab polytheists.
rows.anchor: قوله {والذين أشركوا} يعني مشركي العرب

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَفْصِلُ بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ
rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abū Isḥāq says the first إن takes the whole clause containing the second إن as its predicate.
rows.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: خبر (إن) الأولى جملة الكلام

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَفْصِلُ بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ
rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ allows an إن construction whose predicate begins with another إن when the two subjects differ, citing Arabic usage and 18:30; he disallows matching subjects such as إنك إنك قائم.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: وربما قالت العرب: إن أخاك إن الدين عليه لكثير.

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَفْصِلُ بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ
rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the Basrans unanimously allow إن to enter any subject-predicate construction, so he permits the form al-Farrāʾ had found objectionable.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: وليس بين البصريين خلاف في أن

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَفْصِلُ بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ
rows.speaker: صاحب النظم
rows.claim: The author of al-Naẓm says the long intervening clause makes the first إن seem dropped, so it is repeated with the answer to mark their connection and reinforce the explanation.
rows.anchor: وقال صاحب النظم: لما قال {إن الذين آمنوا}

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَفْصِلُ بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ
rows.speaker: صاحب النظم
rows.claim: He also says the repeated mention of God’s name preserves the ordering of the opening and answer, placing God first as the judge between the named groups.
rows.anchor: على نظم: إن الله يفصل

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَفْصِلُ بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains faṣl as God’s judgment between the groups on Resurrection Day.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يقضي بينهم يوم القيامة

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَفْصِلُ بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَ ٱلْقِيَٰمَةِ
rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says this judgment admits believers to Paradise and the others to Hell, citing the following descriptions of the disbelievers and believers.
rows.anchor: وفسر الزجاج هذا الفصل والقضاء بين هؤلاء الفرق

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍۢ شَهِيدٌ
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says God is witness over the factions’ deeds and knows what is in their hearts.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: شهيد على ما في قلوبهم عالم به

words: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍۢ شَهِيدٌ
rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: The scholars of meaning say God judges religious disputes on Resurrection Day so the truth is made undeniable: the just face turns white and the false claimant’s dark.
rows.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني: إن الله -عز وجل-

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shahīd means knowledge of what is witnessed; God already knows everything before it exists and is Knower of the unseen.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الشهيد: العلم بما شاهده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alam tara means ‘have you not known’: the seeing intended is by the heart, as explained earlier at 2:243.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: {ألم تر} ألم تعلم؛ لأن المراد الرؤية بالقلب

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ takes ‘those in the heavens’ as the inhabitants of heaven and ‘those on earth’ as every created kind, including mountains, jinn, and the like.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: يعني أهل السموات

words: وَٱلشَّمْسُ وَٱلْقَمَرُ وَٱلنُّجُومُ وَٱلْجِبَالُ وَٱلشَّجَرُ وَٱلدَّوَآبُّ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author’s preferred meaning of the listed beings’ prostration is their submission, humility, and obedience to what their Lord wills.
rows.anchor: والصحيح أن المراد بسجودها خضوعها وذلتها

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj says sujūd here is submission to God, an obedience shared by living beings and inanimate things; he cites their response in 41:11.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: السجود هاهنا الخضوع لله

rows.speaker: النحاس
rows.claim: Al-Naḥḥās calls submission the sound reading: everything complies in its created state and in what God gives, heals, or afflicts; this is not worship-prostration.
rows.anchor: وقال النحاس: هذا القول صحيح بين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second group says the design and subjection of nonrational beings themselves summon the informed observer to prostrate; the author says this amounts to the first view, since these are their humility before the Creator.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: إن السجود من هذه الأشياء التي هو موات

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: A poetic line says hills prostrate under hooves, meaning that they bend or are humbled by the hoofbeats; it evidences figurative sujūd for nonrational things.
rows.anchor: الشاعر (¬2): ترى الأكم فيها سجدا للحوافر

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says the shadows of inanimate things and everything except believers turn as their prostration, as in 13:15; scholars relate this to the sun’s course as a sign.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: سجود الجماد وكل شيء سوى المؤمنين

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya says every star, sun, and moon prostrates at setting and waits for permission before returning to its rising place.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو العالية: ما في السماء نجم ولا شمس ولا قمر إلا يقع لله ساجدا حين يغيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this account all creation truly prostrates to God, though people do not know how; he supports this with other verses about stones, mountains, and creation’s praise.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا فكل شيء مما خلقه

rows.speaker: أرباب الأصول
rows.claim: The theologians of uṣūl say inanimate things cannot reason or distinguish; if they display discernment, God must create that capacity, since it is otherwise impossible in their original nature.
rows.anchor: وقال أرباب الأصول: الجمادات لا تعقل ولا يتميز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The many people who prostrate are believers who worship God.
rows.anchor: قوله تعالى: {وكثير من الناس} يعني المؤمنين الذين يسجدون لله تعالى

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says those deserving punishment are unbelievers whose shadows still prostrate; on this reading they too belong among the prostrators.
rows.anchor: يسجد لله ظله، قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view ends the prostration description at ‘the beasts’ and begins a new sentence with ‘many people’; Ibn ʿAbbās says these many are in Paradise, while his ʿAṭāʾ report distinguishes monotheists from those punished for not affirming oneness.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: تم الكلام في وصف الساجدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view ends the sentence at ‘many people’ and starts anew: those punished refused to prostrate and are outside the group of prostrators.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون؛ التمام عند قوله {وكثير من الناس}

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ argues that ‘punishment became due’ implies that many people refused prostration, since punishment is due only for abandoning it.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: قوله {حق عليه العذاب} يدل على أن المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers the pause after ‘many people,’ the stopping choice of Nāfiʿ, al-Kisāʾī, and Abū Ḥātim.
rows.anchor: وهذا القول هو اختيار نافع والكسائي وأبي حاتم

words: وَمَن يُهِنِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِن مُّكْرِمٍ
rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ glosses God’s humiliating someone as making him wretched, with no one to help him; Ibn ʿAbbās is also reported to say this.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: يريد من يشقه الله فما له من مسعد

words: وَمَن يُهِنِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِن مُّكْرِمٍ
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In ʿAṭāʾ’s transmission, Ibn ʿAbbās says this is someone who treats worship of God lightly: God has disgraced and banished him, leaving Hell rather than the honor given to His allies.
rows.anchor: وكذا روى عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does as He wills among His creatures, granting humiliation or honor, misery or happiness.
rows.anchor: أي: في خلقه من الإهانة والكرامة والشقاء والسعادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative pronoun is genitive, with the sense ‘permission was given to those expelled from their homes,’ continuing the preceding verse.
rows.anchor: المعنى: أذن للذين أخرجوا من ديارهم

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ and al-Zajjāj say the monotheists were expelled by idolaters because they proclaimed God’s oneness; ‘they were expelled’ is understood from the opening and the exception.
rows.anchor: الزجاج (¬4): أي لم يخرجوا إلا بأن

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sībawayh treats the exception as disconnected: the sense is ‘but because they say, Our Lord is God,’ meaning they were expelled for monotheism; al-Farrāʾ also records this option.
rows.anchor: وقال سيبويه: هذا من الاستثناء المنقطع

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ also permits construing أن as an exception, as in 92:20.
rows.anchor: وذكر الفراء هذا القول أيضا، فقال: وإن شئت جعلت

words: بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ إِلَّآ أَن يَقُولُوا۟ رَبُّنَا ٱللَّهُ
rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad reports another view: they were expelled on the pretext that their saying ‘Our Lord is God’ entitled them to expulsion, an injustice expressed as a connected exception.
rows.anchor: وحكى المبرد عن بعضهم قولا آخر، وهو: أن المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The connected exception excludes monotheism from wrongdoing for emphatic effect, like al-Nābigha’s ironic exception of sword nicks from a list of faults: these exiles had no real offense.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا الاستثناء متصل، واستثنى التوحيد من الباطل لضرب من المبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is also read difāʿ Allāh, ‘God’s defense’; the author refers readers to the discussion in the preceding verse.
rows.anchor: وقوله: {ولولا دفع الله الناس بعضهم ببعض} وقرئ:

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī allows difāʿ as a verbal noun from triliteral dafaʿa, like kitāb from kataba, rather than a Form III verbal noun; examples include qiyām and ghiyāth.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي: ويجوز أن يكون الدفاع من دفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hadm means demolishing a structure; the noun can also mean what has been demolished.
rows.anchor: وقوله: {لهدمت} الهدم: مصدر هدمت البناء، إذا نقضته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is read with a light or doubled dāl: the light form can cover little or much demolition, while the doubled form is specific to extensive demolition.
rows.anchor: فالتخفيف يكون للكثير والقليل، يدلك على ذلك أنك تقول

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: Al-Azharī defines ṣawāmiʿ as hermits’ monasteries, named for their tapered tops; ṣamaʿa a dish means raising and sharpening its top, and aṣmaʿ describes a keen-witted man.
rows.anchor: قال الأزهري: الصومعة من البناء سميت صومعة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid and al-Ḍaḥḥāk identify the ṣawāmiʿ as monks’ monasteries.
rows.anchor: مجاهد، والضحاك (¬6): يعني صوامع

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda says the ṣawāmiʿ belong to the Ṣābians.
rows.anchor: قتادة: الصوامع للصابئين (¬1)

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
rows.claim: Muqātil ibn Ḥayyān identifies them as buildings beside roads.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل بن حيان: هي البيوت التي على الطرق
